## Introduction

This page lists further resources for learning about the topics covered in this course,
and for learning more about related topics.
Required readings and optional self-study resources from the pages for each week are
also repeated here, so that you can find them all in one place.

## Reproducibility

#### General

- [Good enough practices in scientific computing](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005510){target="_blank"}
(Wilson et al. 2017, PLoS Computational Biology)
- [Reproducible Research: A Retrospective](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33467923/){target="_blank"}
  (Peng & Hicks 2021, Annu Rev Public Health)
- [Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285){target="_blank"}
  (Sandve et al. 2013, PLoS Computational Biology)
- [The Turing Way](https://book.the-turing-way.org/){target="_blank"} --
  A community handbook on reproducible, collaborative data science.
- [Openness and Computational Reproducibility in Plant Pathology: Where We Stand and a Way Forward](https://doi.org/10.1094/PHYTO-10-21-0430-PER){target="_blank"}
  (Sparks et al. 2023, Phytopathology)
- [Open access and reproducibility in plant pathology research: Guidelines and best practices](https://doi.org/10.1094/PHYTO-12-23-0483-IA){target="_blank"}
  (Grünwald et al. 2024, Phytopathology)
- [The five pillars of computational reproducibility: bioinformatics and beyond](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbad375){target="_blank"}
  (Ziemann et al. 2023, Briefings in Bioinformatics)
- [Five selfish reasons to work reproducibly](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-015-0850-7){target="_blank"}
  (Markowetz 2015, Genome Biology)
- [A quick guide to organizing computational biology projects](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1000424){target="_blank"}
  (Noble 2009, PLoS Computational Biology)

#### Data management and documentation

- [The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18){target="_blank"}
  (Wilkinson et al. 2016, Scientific Data)
- [What's in a README?](https://blog.datadryad.org/2025/09/09/whats-in-a-readme-why-your-readme-matters-and-how-to-create-the-best-one-possible/){target="_blank"}
  (Dryad blog), and a
  [README template for datasets](https://cornell.app.box.com/v/ReadmeTemplate){target="_blank"}
  (Cornell University)
- [Project structure](https://djnavarro.net/slides-project-structure/){target="_blank"}
  (slides by Danielle Navarro)

## Shell

#### Online guides and tutorials

- [sandbox.bio](https://sandbox.bio){target="_blank"} --
  Interactive bioinformatics tutorials, including on shell basics, that run in your browser.
- [Command Challenge](https://cmdchallenge.com/){target="_blank"} --
  shell puzzles to solve in your browser.
- Nice collections of one-liners, mostly for bioinformatics
  - [By Bonnie I-Man Ng](https://onceupon.github.io/Bash-Oneliner/){target="_blank"}
  - [By Stephen Turner](https://github.com/stephenturner/oneliners/blob/master/README.md){target="_blank"}
  - [By Tommy Ming](https://github.com/crazyhottommy/bioinformatics-one-liners){target="_blank"}
  - [By Amy Williams](http://williamslab.bscb.cornell.edu/?page_id=235){target="_blank"}

#### Books

- [The Linux Command Line: A Complete Introduction](https://library.ohio-state.edu/record=b8640501~S7){target="_blank"}
  (William Shotts, 2019)
- [Linux Command Line and Shell Scripting Bible](https://library.ohio-state.edu/record=b9161748~S7){target="_blank"}

- [Command Line Kung Fu](https://www.amazon.com/dp/1499222033){target="_blank"} (Jason Cannon, 2014)

#### Further reading

- [Ten simple rules for getting started with command-line bioinformatics](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008645){target="_blank"}
  (Brandies & Hogg 2021, PLoS Computational Biology)
- [Five reasons why researchers should learn to love the command line](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-021-00263-0){target="_blank"}

## Git

#### Online guides and tutorials -- general

- [An overview of Git tutorials](https://gist.github.com/jaseemabid/1321592){target="_blank"}
- [Happy Git and GitHub for the useR](https://happygitwithr.com/){target="_blank"}
  Somewhat R-centric, but a very accessible introduction to Git.
- [Git best practices](https://sethrobertson.github.io/GitBestPractices/){target="_blank"} by Seth Robertson
- [Atlassian Git tutorials](https://www.atlassian.com/git/tutorials/what-is-version-control){target="_blank"}
- A quick [GitHub overview](https://guides.github.com/activities/hello-world/){target="_blank"}
  of some Git and GitHub functionality including branching and Pull Requests

#### Online guides and tutorials -- interactive practice

- [Git-it](https://github.com/jlord/git-it-electron#git-it){target="_blank"} -- a small application to learn and practice Git and GitHub basics.
- [Learn Git branching](https://learngitbranching.js.org/){target="_blank"}
- [GitHub Skills](https://skills.github.com/){target="_blank"} -- short interactive courses
  on using GitHub, which take place in a GitHub repository.

#### Further reading

- [A Quick Introduction to Version Control with Git and GitHub](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004668){target="_blank"}
  (Blischak et al. 2016, PLoS Computational Biology)
- [Not just for programmers: How GitHub can accelerate collaborative and reproducible research in ecology and evolution](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.14108){target="_blank"}
  (Braga et al. 2023, Methods in Ecology and Evolution)
- [Excuse me, do you have a moment to talk about version control?](https://peerj.com/preprints/3159/){target="_blank"} (Bryan 2017, PeerJ)
- [Ten Simple Rules for Taking Advantage of Git and GitHub](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pcbi.1004947){target="_blank"}
  (Perez-Riverol et al. 2016, PLoS Comutational Biology)

## R

### Books

- [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/){target="_blank"} (Wickham et al.) --
  The standard introduction to the tidyverse.
- [R for Plant Disease Epidemiology](https://r4pde.netlify.app/){target="_blank"} (Emerson Del Ponte et al.)
- [Fundamentals of Data Visualization](https://clauswilke.com/dataviz/){target="_blank"} (Claus Wilke) --
  About principles of good figures rather than code.
- [R Graphics Cookbook](https://r-graphics.org/){target="_blank"} (Winston Chang)

### Courses and tutorials

- [R for Bio Data Science](https://r4bds.github.io/){target="_blank"} (Technical University of Denmark)
- [STAT 545](https://stat545.com/){target="_blank"} (Jenny Bryan)
- [R Crash Course for Biologists](https://quantitative.bio/R-Crash-Course/){target="_blank"}

## General/similar courses and books

#### Courses

- [Practical Computing and Bioinformatics for Conservation and Evolutionary Genomics](https://eriqande.github.io/eca-bioinf-handbook/){target="_blank"}
  (Eric Anderson) -- Covers the shell, HPC with Slurm, Git, and R.
- [Tools for Reproducible Research](https://kbroman.org/Tools4RR/pages/schedule.html){target="_blank"}
  (Karl Broman, University of Wisconsin--Madison)
- [Computing Tools for Data Analytics](https://cecileane.github.io/computingtools/){target="_blank"}
  (Cécile Ané, University of Wisconsin--Madison)
- [The Missing Semester of Your CS Education](https://missing.csail.mit.edu/){target="_blank"}
  -- An MIT course on the shell, scripting, editors, Git, and more.
- [Omics Data Analysis](https://uclouvain-cbio.github.io/WSBIM2122/){target="_blank"}
  (Laurent Gatto, course)
- [Introduction to Bioinformatics and Computational Biology by Shirley Liu](https://liulab-dfci.github.io/bioinfo-combio/){target="_blank"}
- [Applied Genomics course by Michael Schatz](https://github.com/schatzlab/appliedgenomics2020){target="_blank"}
- [Applied Computational Genomics course by Aaron Quinlan](https://github.com/quinlan-lab/applied-computational-genomics){target="_blank"}
- [Modern Plain Text Computing](https://mptc.io/){target="_blank"} (Kieran Healy)

#### Books

- [Computing Skills for Biologists](https://search.library.osu.edu/permalink/01OHIOLINK_OSU/1n8rc7n/alma991085862322008507){target="_blank"}

- [Computational Genomics with R](https://compgenomr.github.io/book/){target="_blank"}

## Omics data

#### Introductory papers

- [Working with omics data: An interdisciplinary challenge at the crossroads of biology and computer science](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-0716-3195-9_10){target="_blank"}
  (Poinsignon et al. 2023, in _Machine Learning for Brain Disorders_)
- [The principles and applications of high-throughput sequencing technologies](https://doi.org/10.12717/DR.2023.27.1.9){target="_blank"}
  (Lee 2023, Development & Reproduction)
- [High-throughput sequencing in plant disease management: a comprehensive review of benefits, challenges, and future perspectives](https://doi.org/10.1186/s42483-023-00199-5){target="_blank"}
  (Nizamani et al. 2023, Phytopathology Research)
- [New-generation sequencing technology in diagnosis of fungal plant pathogens: A dream comes true?](https://doi.org/10.3390/jof8070737){target="_blank"}
  (Aragona et al. 2022, Journal of Fungi)
- [Multi-omics revolution to promote plant breeding efficiency](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2022.1062952){target="_blank"}
  (Mahmood et al. 2022, Frontiers in Plant Science)
- [Sequencing-based analysis of microbiomes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41576-024-00746-6){target="_blank"}
  (Pinto & Bhatt 2024, Nature Reviews Genetics)
- [Genome, transcriptome and proteome: the rise of omics data and their integration in biomedical sciences](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbw114){target="_blank"}
  (Manzoni et al. 2018, Briefings in Bioinformatics)
- [Advancing species conservation and management through omics tools](https://doi.org/10.1111/1755-0998.14123){target="_blank"}
  (von der Heyden et al. 2025, Molecular Ecology Resources)

#### Example dataset

- [Two avian _Plasmodium_ species trigger different transcriptional responses on their vector _Culex pipiens_](https://doi.org/10.1111/mec.17240){target="_blank"}
  (Garrigós et al. 2025, Molecular Ecology) ---
  the paper behind the course's example dataset.
